To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spray process can be applied to form Au nanoparticles for the fabrication of plasmonic IOSCs with improved performance.
the spray technique can be used for the direct formation and deposition of gold nanoparticles for improving the performance of inverted solar cells.

the application of electric field in the spray process resulted the formation of smaller Au nanoparticles (35 nm as against 70 nm without electric field) with more uniform distribution, which in turn resulted in a difference in the SPR effect created by the Au nanoparticles and affected the solar cell performances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the electric field applied during the spray deposition of Au nanoparticles on the plasmonic effect in inverted organic solar cell.
the study of the effect of Au nanoparticles on the efficiency of IOSC.
the fabrication of plasmonic IOSCs by the spray technique and the study of the effect of the size and the distribution of Au nanoparticles on their performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of electric field in the spray process is a promising approach for the preparation of Au NPs and their application in IOSC.
, in order to improve the efficiency of the solar cells by the plasmonic effect, it is necessary to have a good SPR effect.

the application of the electric field during the spraying process resulted in the formation of smaller sized Au NPs with more uniform distribution and hence the plasmonic effect of the Au NPs was found to have a strong impact on the solar cell performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasmonic Au nanoparticles can be used to enhance the performance of IOSC by the spray process.
the spray technique can be applied in the fabrication of Au nanoparticles in IOSC for the enhancement of the performance of the IOSC with the help of plasmonic effects.

the spray-deposited gold nanoparticles with the application of electric field (1 kV) in the inverted organic solar cells can provide a simple, effective, and scalable method for the fabrication of efficient plasmonic organic solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the application of an external electric field during the deposition of Au nanoparticles by the spray process can result in smaller size and more uniform distribution of Au nanoparticles which in turn can be utilized for plasmonic applications.
the application of electric field in the spray process is very effective for the formation of uniform and small size of Au nanoparticles.
the spray technique can be applied for the direct deposition of gold nanoparticles in the fabrication process of inverted organic solar cell with improved performance.
